comparisons.peer_topic: Other Income (Expense), Net Composition and Results
comparisons.peer_summary: Other income (expense), net totaled $181 million in 2024, down from $197 million in 2023, primarily due to decreased interest income from lower short-term investment balances; this line item is primarily comprised of interest income from short-term investments, changes in valuation of equity investments, and foreign currency transaction gains and losses.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD disclose drivers for their respective 'other/investment income' lines, focusing on the interplay between interest rates and investment balances, but with opposite volume trends. QCOM reports an increase in income driven by both higher balances and higher rates. In contrast, AMD reports a decrease in income, driven specifically by lower investment balances, despite the high-rate environment; AMD also explicitly includes non-interest items like equity valuation changes and foreign currency gains, whereas QCOM's summary isolates interest-bearing securities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Other income net decrease due to lower invested balance
comparisons.peer_summary: Other income, net decreased to $406 million in fiscal year 2024 from $512 million in 2023, primarily due to lower interest income resulting from a lower invested balance.
comparisons.comparison: QCOM and AVGO both attribute changes in their other/investment income primarily to interest income fluctuations resulting from changes in invested balances. AVGO explicitly states that its decrease in income was due to a 'lower invested balance.' QCOM’s increase was due to 'higher balances' of interest-bearing securities. This highlights a direct comparative contrast in balance sheet positioning (expanding vs. contracting invested balances) driving opposite income trends in a similar high-rate environment.
